_comment: The ticket-checkout probe's fixture — MOT-711.
Deliberately the SAME org and event as the deployed ticket-checkout matrix
(website/e2e/deployed/ticket-checkout/fixtures.json), which is the opposite
of the choice the SHOP made: its probe buys a dedicated SKU so a probe run
can never move a suite's stock.
The reason the trade inverts here is that this probe WRITES NOTHING — see
the header of scripts/ticket-checkout-probe.mjs. With no reservation and no
order, there is no stock to interfere with, and pointing the probe at the
same fixture the suite depends on is strictly better: the probe then
reports on the exact fixture whose rot would take the suite down, twice a
day, instead of reporting on a fixture nobody else uses.
`zeroSeatTierName` is the tier the probe drives the REFUSAL half against.
It is held at zero available by the seeder, which is what makes a create
attempt exercise routing, auth, the event load, the tier lookup and the
availability guard while reserving nothing.
It was called `soldOutTierName` / `E2E Sold Out` until MOT-743. The tier's
NAME is interpolated into every refusal `createOrder` raises, so a name
containing the words the probe matched on made the probe's own
"the availability guard is what answered" check answer yes for a refusal
from anywhere. Renamed, and the check is now anchored on the exact refusal
sentence and its 409 — see step 4 of scripts/ticket-checkout-probe.mjs.
`sellableTierName` is the tier the probe BUYS from. Since MOT-735 shipped
`POST /orders/:orderId/probe-cancel`, the probe creates a real order and
cancels it, so it now reaches the PaymentIntent and the inventory write —
the two things the refusal half deliberately stops short of.
